reason: The sources provide over 15 corroborating facts across seven independent sites detailing the Artemis II mission profile, crew, hardware, and milestones.
story: More than half a century after Apollo 17, NASA launched Artemis II from Kennedy Space Center, carrying four astronauts on a landmark ten-day journey around the Moon. Flying aboard the Orion spacecraft—christened Integrity—commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen became the first lunar travelers of the twenty-first century. Hansen made history as the first Canadian and non-American to venture beyond low Earth orbit. Propelled by the massive Space Launch System and powered by the European Service Module, the crew tested life-support systems, practiced manual proximity maneuvers against their spent upper stage in high Earth orbit, and flew a precision free-return trajectory around the Moon's far side without entering lunar orbit. Traveling farther into deep space than any human beings before them, the crew demonstrated critical systems for future lunar landings before executing a fiery Pacific Ocean splashdown.
angle: On Artemis II, four astronauts ventured farther into deep space than any humans in history, flying on a free-return slingshot around the lunar far side to shatter Apollo 13's all-time distance record.

claims.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The mission sends four astronauts on an approximately 10-day circumlunar test flight around the Moon and back to Earth.
Artemis II launched atop the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The astronauts flew aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft, named 'Integrity' by the crew.
The crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Reid Wiseman served as mission commander and Victor Glover served as pilot.
Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen served as mission specialists on the flight.
Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency became the first non-American astronaut to travel beyond low Earth orbit to the Moon.
The European Space Agency supplied the European Service Module (ESM), which provides Orion with propulsion, electrical power, water, and life support.
Artemis II followed a lunar free-return trajectory that loops around the Moon without entering lunar orbit.
In high Earth orbit, the crew took manual control of Orion to conduct a proximity operations demonstration using the spent upper stage (ICPS) as a target.
The flight traveled farther into deep space from Earth than any previous crewed mission in history.
The rocket's upper stage deployed four secondary CubeSats from international partners including Germany, Argentina, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea.
The spacecraft carried the AVATAR payload to study human health and tissue analog responses in deep space.
During the translunar flight on Easter weekend, pilot Victor Glover delivered a broadcast describing Earth as a fragile oasis in space.
NASA officially announced the four-person Artemis II crew at Ellington Field near Houston, Texas.
Jared Isaacman served as the NASA Administrator during the mission's preparation and flight.
The mission concluded with splashdown in the Pacific Ocean and recovery operations conducted by NASA and the U.S. Navy.

disputed: Closest approach distance to the Moon varies across sources: S1 lists an altitude of approximately 4,067 miles (6,545 km) above the far-side lunar surface, S4 reports an approach within 6,479 miles (10,427 km) of the lunar surface, and S3 reports flying almost 7,500 km beyond the Moon. Scripts should refer broadly to a flyby several thousand miles above the lunar far side.
Orion's high Earth orbit apogee is cited as roughly 44,000 miles in S1 but approximately 46,000 miles in S2. Scripts should state the orbit apogee was between 44,000 and 46,000 miles.

Target launch windows shifted over time across sources, from late 2024 (S4) to 2025 (S6, S7), February 2026 (S1, S7), and finally April 2026 (S1, S2, S3). Scripts should mention that the launch date faced repeated delays and target adjustments due to hardware testing.
